concerns.text: Success Criterion SC-009 (power analysis confirming detection capability with ≥ 10 000 realizations) is not anchored to any User Story or Functional Requirement; no FR describes a power‑analysis task, leaving this SC orphaned.

FR-004 requires generating ≥ 10 000 ΛCDM Gaussian random realizations, but Constitution VI (FR-030) mandates validation against exactly 1 000 realizations. This direct conflict makes the required simulation count ambiguous and violates the higher‑level constitutional rule.

Functional requirements reference user‑story identifiers US-1, US-2, US-3, yet the User Stories are only labeled “User Story 1”, “User Story 2”, “User Story 3” without explicit US‑1/US‑2/US‑3 IDs. The cross‑references cannot be resolved, breaking traceability.

FR-012 specifies that the system must compute a theoretical ISW cross‑correlation curve using CAMB/CLASS and output a CSV, but it does not define how the correctness of that curve will be verified. No measurable validation (e.g., comparison to published reference values, tolerance thresholds, or schema checks on the curve shape) is provided, making the requirement untestable.

FR-007 requires detection of redshift gaps, masking, and logging a warning, yet the specification does not provide a reachable test input or fixture that guarantees a redshift‑gap scenario. Without an explicit synthetic or curated dataset that contains a known gap, the edge case cannot be reliably exercised in automated tests.

FR-008 mandates graceful handling of the case where no cold‑spot candidates meet the –2σ threshold, returning an empty list and p‑value = 1.0. The spec does not describe a deterministic way to trigger this condition (e.g., a synthetic CMB map with no pixels below –2σ). Absence of a guaranteed input makes the test non‑reproducible.

FR-004 requires ≥ 10 000 ΛCDM realizations, but the original idea specifies 1 000 realizations (and the Constitution (VI) mandates exactly 1 000). This exceeds the scope of the idea and violates the project constitution.

FR-012 adds computation of a theoretical ISW cross‑correlation curve (CAMB/CLASS linear‑theory model). The idea never requested a theoretical benchmark; this introduces a new analysis component beyond the stated research question.

FR-005 mandates a full sensitivity sweep with FDR‑adjusted q‑values across 35 parameter combinations. The idea only required a basic cold‑spot detection and cross‑correlation; this sensitivity analysis is not part of the original scope.
FR-020 requires full CI integration and automated testing on each push. The idea did not include CI or continuous testing as a deliverable; this is an engineering addition beyond the research scope.
FR-019 demands schema validation of all output artifacts. While good practice, schema validation was not part of the original idea and adds unnecessary scope.

FR-021 specifies a JSON output file conforming to a schema. The idea only required correlation plots, a p‑value table, and a reproducible notebook; the JSON artifact is an extra deliverable not requested.
FR-016 introduces a synthetic oversized HEALPix map fixture to trigger a memory‑pressure abort path. This testing fixture was not mentioned in the idea and adds complexity beyond the needed analysis.

SC-004 defines a χ² goodness‑of‑fit test between the observed cross‑correlation ξ(θ) and the theoretical ISW curve, requiring χ²/ndf ≤ 1.5 (p≥0.05). The specification does not provide per‑bin uncertainty estimates (σ_i) for ξ(θ), nor does it describe how the covariance between angular bins is handled. Without well‑defined variances or a covariance matrix, the χ² statistic is not statistically valid, making the validation of the ISW hypothesis circularly dependent on an ill‑specified error model.

new_concerns.text: SC-009 (power analysis confirming detection capability with ≥ 10 000 realizations) is absent. The specification only performs a power analysis with 1 000 realizations (FR‑023), which does not satisfy the previously raised requirement for ≥ 10 000 realizations.

Power analysis (SC-009 / FR-023) claims ≥80 % detection power for an ISW amplitude ≥ 0.5 µK using only the 1 000 ΛCDM Gaussian random realizations. The specification does not describe generating signal‑injected (alternative‑hypothesis) simulations, so the power claim relies on the null simulations alone, making the validation potentially circular.
